s1.syndrome_frame: Obstructive sleep disorder with upper airway obstruction
salient_findings: Cystic mass at the base of the tongue
key_facts: Excessive daytime somnolence (Epworth Sleepiness Scale score 13)
20×20 mm round cystic mass at the base of the tongue
33×31×27 mm well-defined cystic lesion in the midline of the tongue base

raw.syndrome_frame: Obstructive sleep disorder with upper airway obstruction
salient_findings: Cystic mass at the base of the tongue
key_facts: Excessive daytime somnolence (Epworth Sleepiness Scale score 13)
20×20 mm round cystic mass at the base of the tongue
33×31×27 mm well-defined cystic lesion in the midline of the tongue base

shortlist.label: Thyroglossal duct cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass at the base of the tongue, consistent with thyroglossal duct cyst location and characteristics

shortlist.label: Ranula
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic lesion in the tongue base, possible ranula given the location and cystic nature

shortlist.label: Dermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Well-defined cystic lesion, dermoid cyst is a plausible diagnosis given the imaging characteristics

shortlist.label: Lingual thyroid
shortlist.why_kept: Mass at the base of the tongue, lingual thyroid is a rare but possible cause of upper airway obstruction

shortlist.label: Lymphangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic lesion with potential for lymphatic malformation, lymphangioma is a possible diagnosis given the clinical presentation

raw.rationale: The presence of a 20×20 mm round cystic mass at the base of the tongue and a 33×31×27 mm well-defined cystic lesion in the midline of the tongue base on CT scan, along with symptoms of obstructive sleep apnea and voice change, are consistent with a thyroglossal duct cyst, which is a congenital anomaly that can present as a midline neck mass and can cause airway obstruction.

rejected.label: Ranula
rejected.why: Ranula typically presents as a blue, translucent lesion in the floor of the mouth, not at the base of the tongue

rejected.label: Dermoid cyst
rejected.why: Dermoid cysts are typically found in the midline of the neck, but are not usually associated with airway obstruction

rejected.label: Lingual thyroid
rejected.why: Lingual thyroid would likely be associated with thyroid function abnormalities, which are not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Lymphangioma
rejected.why: Lymphangioma is a rare congenital anomaly that can present as a neck mass, but is not typically associated with the specific symptoms and imaging findings in this case
